claims.text: A single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti high-entropy alloy has coercivity below 10 Oe.
The low coercivity of the single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy is associated with suppressed orbital moments.
Intermediate-temperature annealing or cold rolling followed by aging can induce a nanoscale coherent BCC secondary phase in an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The induced BCC phase will be enriched in Ti and Cr, if Cr is present, or will consist of Ti-rich clusters.
The fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix remains ferromagnetically ordered from approximately 300 K to 600 K.
The secondary BCC phase remains antiferromagnetic or weakly ferromagnetic and has high magnetic anisotropy over the operating range.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates and coherent dual-phase structures can be created in compositionally complex alloys.
Coherent fcc/BCC interfaces in the proposed alloy act as magnetic domain-wall pinning sites.
The fcc/BCC interfaces mediate exchange-spring coupling between the soft ferromagnetic fcc matrix and hard antiferromagnetic or weakly ferromagnetic BCC precipitates.
Antiferromagnetic BCC precipitates or Ti-induced magnetocrystalline anisotropy increase the local anisotropy energy.
Interface pinning and exchange coupling require a larger external field for magnetization reversal.
Introducing the secondary BCC phase will raise coercivity above 100 Oe.
The coercivity enhancement above 100 Oe will persist at room temperature and elevated temperatures.
Formation of the secondary phase will lower saturation magnetization relative to the single-phase alloy.
The resulting saturation magnetization will remain significantly higher than that of a fully antiferromagnetic system.
The magnetic ordering temperature of the dual-phase alloy is determined by the ferromagnetic fcc matrix.
The absence of secondary phases and low anisotropy in the single-phase alloy permit easy domain-wall motion.
The coercivity-enhancing effect requires the BCC phase to remain coherent and smaller than 100 nm.
Coarsened or incoherent BCC precipitates may dilute the magnetic phase or introduce cracks, reducing coercivity or mechanical integrity.
The proposed coercivity enhancement operates only below the Curie temperature of the fcc matrix.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the hypothesis applies only when the BCC phase is coherent and nanoscale, but the falsification rule treats an absent or incoherent BCC phase as falsifying the hypothesis. Such a specimen represents failure to realize the stated intervention or lies outside the hypothesis's applicability, rather than decisively testing the claimed effect of a coherent dual-phase structure.
